rows.text: A salty smell drifted from the hams; apparently, even after death, flesh was expected to keep improving itself.
A hanging ham turned slightly, presenting its better side. Even here, being dead did not excuse anyone from looking marketable.
The machine breathed a little warmth into the air; Gerald declined to contribute. Bitterness was clearly a craft here, and the coffee was still learning.
The machine gave a self-important hiss. Gerald let it finish; winning his friendship had apparently been easier for you than for something that had worked beside him for years.
Flick edged away from the crack, apparently unwilling to be illuminated by anything with such a poor record of holding water.
The light briefly brightens, then dims with the discretion of a rumour that has discovered it might be true.
Portia gave a faint stone-on-stone creak, achieving the rare architectural feat of looking down on someone while remaining an entrance. Being open was evidently not the same as being welcoming.
The smoke smelled faintly of scorched certainty. Having warmed to you, the archway now confined its identity crisis to the space above your head, which counted as hospitality.
A sliver of light settled on a book spine, which immediately looked less available. The shop understood that the first rule of selling books was to make being bought seem slightly beneath them.
A cool draft slipped between the books, which made no effort to look available. Being bought was apparently something that happened to lesser literature.
A faint smell of dry wood rose from the roots. The branch was dead, but apparently that was no excuse for lying down.
A root nudged the edge of the light, claiming another inch. The market had ended, but this had done nothing to discourage expansion.
